'''Piangil''', once frequently spelled "Pyangil", is a town in the [[The Mallee|Mallee]] region of northern [[Victoria (Australia)|Victoria]], [[Australia]]. It is approximately {{convert|382|km|mi|0}} north-west of the state capital, [[Melbourne]] and {{convert|46|km|mi}} north-west of the regional centre of [[Swan Hill]]. At the {{CensusAU|2016}}, Piangil and the surrounding rural area had a population of 259.<ref name=ABS2016/>

The name of the town is derived from the Piangil [[pastoralism|pastoral]] run, taken up in 1846 by [[William Coghill]]. It is thought that the name was derived from an [[Aboriginal Australians|Aboriginal]] word for the [[Murray cod]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Piangil |url=https://www.victorianplaces.com.au/piangil |website=Victorian Places |access-date=2025-05-14}}</ref>

Piangil post office opened on 17 June 1907, and was renamed Piangil North in 1918 when the Piangil post office was relocated adjacent to the railway station. A new Piangil post office opened in 1921 and is still in operation.<ref name = "a">{{Citation | last = Phoenix Auctions History  | title = Post Office List | url = http://www.phoenixauctions.com.au/cgi-bin/wsPhoenix.sh/Viewpocdwrapper.p?SortBy=VIC&filter=*Piangil* | access-date = 2 April 2021}}</ref>

Piangil Primary School closed in September 2015.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.weeklytimesnow.com.au/news/small-school-closures-continue-in-rural-victoria/news-story/35f1193bf26c4d9a040ecb7d45641964 |last1=Twomey |first1=Shannon |last2=Zervos |first2=Cassie |title=Small school closures continue in rural Victoria |work=The Weekly Times |date=5 November 2015 |access-date=31 January 2019}}</ref>
